minor.issue: Failed tiles are recorded with attempts/backoff but no timer schedules updateHighResolutionTiles after 4s/8s. A retry happens only if some unrelated zoom/style/dataset update later calls the renderer, so a stationary view can retain a silent gap indefinitely despite the retry claim. Reproduced by focused source-contract pytest.

action_items: In each failed tile's error path, schedule a bounded retry that calls updateHighResolutionTiles after the current 4000*attempts delay (and prevent stale/duplicate timers as needed); then rerun iteration_4 pytest and overlay shell checks.

Validate clipboard connect, Steam/device authorization, voice reconnect timing, crash-file emission/pruning, and secondary-monitor restore on Windows because WPF runtime execution is unavailable in this Linux environment.
critical_code_review_comments: The tile backoff state controls eligibility but not execution: without setTimeout/request scheduling, elapsed backoff alone cannot cause a removed image to be recreated.

ConnectPrivateServerFromClipboardAsync reports success when state is connecting/signing-in as designed, but true end-to-end authorization and final live/error transitions require a Windows test with a relay and Steam flow.

rca_of_the_issue: On tile error, index.html increments failedGatewayTiles and removes the SVG image. updateHighResolutionTiles correctly refuses recreation until Date.now()-failure.at reaches 4000*attempts, but nothing invokes that function when the interval expires. Only setTerrainDataset or a layer style mutation invokes it, so retry is event-driven by unrelated activity rather than automatic. Reproduction: pytest /app/tests/test_private_server_improvements.py::test_failed_tiles_schedule_an_automatic_retry_after_error.
